title: Superhost Rating Figure for Long-Standing Host Accounts
content:
# Host Support Academy — The Rating Figure of a Superhost Decision (Host Accounts)

**Q. How is the rating figure set when the Superhost assessment of an individual Host Accounts holder is decided again?**

By the account's record of met Superhost assessments over its whole history:

- an account with **at least 8** Superhost assessments recorded as met over its whole history: the rating figure is the average of the average ratings recorded at the account's Superhost assessments dated within the **12 months** before the decision;
- an account with **at least 4 but fewer than 8** such assessments: the average of those recorded at its assessments dated within the **6 months** before the decision;
- an account with fewer than 4: the rating figure is not averaged across assessments.

Each average is rounded half up to 2 decimal places. A window of a number of months holds the records dated fewer than that many whole calendar months before the date of the decision.

**Q. Does the count of met assessments look only at the last year?**
No. The 8 and the 4 count met assessments over the account's whole history; the 12 months and the 6 months only say which assessments' ratings are averaged.

**Q. Which assessments enter the average?**
Every Superhost assessment of the account dated within the window, met or not, at the average rating recorded on it.

**Q. A worked case?**
Hypothetically: an account with 9 met assessments over its history has four assessments dated within the 12 months before the decision, recorded at 4.82, 4.85, 4.78 and 4.76 stars. The rating figure is their average, 19.21 divided by 4, which is 4.8025, rounded to **4.80**.

**Q. And at the boundary?**
Exactly 8 met assessments over the history takes the 12-month average; exactly 7 takes the 6-month average; exactly 4 takes the 6-month average; exactly 3 is not averaged.
